prompt:
A golfer hits a golf ball from an elevated tee on a cliff edge, 12.0 m above a level horizontal fairway. The ball is launched with an initial velocity of 26.0 m s^-1 at an angle of 30.0 degrees above the horizontal. Air resistance is negligible. [Use g = 9.81 m s^-2]
[FIGURE PLACEHOLDER: Diagram showing the elevated tee at height 12.0 m above the horizontal fairway. The launch vector is indicated at 26.0 m s^-1 at 30.0 degrees above the horizontal. The curved parabolic trajectory rises to a peak and descends to hit the fairway.]
(a) Show that the initial horizontal component of velocity is 22.5 m s^-1 and the initial vertical component of velocity is 13.0 m s^-1. [2 marks]
(b) Calculate the maximum height reached by the ball above the tee. [2 marks]
(c) Calculate the total time taken for the ball to land on the fairway. [2 marks]

response_structure.description: Calculation of initial horizontal and vertical velocity components.
Calculation of maximum vertical height reached above the tee.
Calculation of total flight time from tee to fairway.

hints: Resolve the 26.0 m s^-1 launch velocity using cos(30 deg) for horizontal and sin(30 deg) for vertical.
common_pitfalls: Swapping sine and cosine functions when resolving components.

hints: At maximum height above the tee, vertical velocity is zero: v_y = 0.
walkthrough: Step 1: Apply v_y^2 = u_y^2 - 2 g h_max with v_y = 0.
Step 3: h_max = 169 / 19.62 = 8.61 m above the tee.
common_pitfalls: Using the total speed 26.0 m s^-1 instead of the vertical component 13.0 m s^-1.
Forgetting that the question asks for height above the tee rather than above the fairway.

hints: Take upwards as positive. The fairway is 12.0 m below the tee, so vertical displacement s_y = -12.0 m.
Set up the quadratic equation s_y = u_y t - 0.5 g t^2 and solve for positive t.
walkthrough: Step 1: Set up displacement equation: -12.0 = 13.0 t - 0.5(9.81) t^2 => 4.905 t^2 - 13.0 t - 12.0 = 0.
common_pitfalls: Taking vertical displacement as positive +12.0 m instead of -12.0 m.
Using total launch velocity 26.0 m s^-1 in the vertical quadratic equation.

hints: Break the motion into independent horizontal and vertical stages.
Remember that the fairway is 12.0 m below the launch height.
teacher_walkthrough: Step 1: In part (a), resolve initial velocity: u_x = 26.0 cos(30.0 deg) = 22.5 m s^-1, u_y = 26.0 sin(30.0 deg) = 13.0 m s^-1 [2 marks].
Step 2: In part (b), at the highest point v_y = 0: 0 = 13.0^2 - 2 x 9.81 x h => h = 8.61 m [2 marks].
Step 3: In part (c), total vertical displacement is s_y = -12.0 m. Solve 4.905 t^2 - 13.0 t - 12.0 = 0 to get t = 3.38 s [2 marks].

provenance.independence_statement: Authored independently to test multipart projectile motion from an elevated launch.
